newsitem.title: FRANCE: Essilor ready for more acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Essilor ready for more acquisitions.

text.p: French lens manufacturer Essilor said on Monday that it was back in the market for acquisitions after having reduced its debt to equity ratio to 29 percent.

"We plan to pursue external growth," chairman Xavier Fontanet told the annual shareholders meeting. "The reduction of our debt ratio to 29 percent leaves us in a position to take up opportunities that present themselves, notably in the United States."
Officials said the group was not currently in bid negotiations.

Essilor's debt rose last year, and its debt-to-equity ratio surged to 43 percent from 20 percent, after it bought four U.S. firms, but it lowered the ratio to 29 percent through bond conversion operations.
Its largest shareholder, Saint Gobain, raised its stake to 25.4 percent of the capital and 31.6 percent of the voting rights through the operations.
Fontanet said Saint Gobain's holding represented "strength and stability". Saint Gobain has five seats on Essilor's 15-member board.
